## Summary of the Patch

This patch fixes a potential out-of-bounds (OOB) font access vulnerability in the fbcon (framebuffer console) rotation code. The bug occurs when `fbcon_rotate_font()` fails to reallocate a larger font buffer during console rotation, but retains the old (undersized) buffer. Subsequent character printing operations that use the rotated font can then overflow the buffer when accessing character data beyond its capacity.

### Modifications in Each File

- **`drivers/video/fbdev/core/fbcon_rotate.c`** (lines 46-60):  
  - Before attempting to allocate a new font buffer, the old buffer is now freed and the pointer (`par->fontbuffer`) and size (`par->fd_size`) are cleared (set to `NULL` and `0`).  
  - The `kfree()` of the old buffer is moved **before** the `kmalloc_array()` call, so that on allocation failure the font data is already discarded instead of leaving an invalid buffer.  
  - The rest of the logic (assigning the new buffer and size on success) remains unchanged.

### Relationships Among the Changes

All changes are confined to a single file and function (`fbcon_rotate_font`). The fix directly reorders the buffer management operations and adds a defensive cleanup: if the reallocation fails, the font buffer is explicitly invalidated. This ensures that any subsequent access to the rotated font (e.g., via `putcs` implementations) will detect the NULL buffer and exit early, preventing an OOB read/write. No other files are affected.
